domain: daily volume/participation and liquidity-shape information: abnormal-volume-without-price-followthrough states across the frozen sector-ETF cohort, with explicit market neutralization

mechanism.causal_story: High participation carries different information depending on whether price follows it. When a sector's participation is abnormally high while its trailing price move is small, motivated flow is being absorbed by patient liquidity (accumulation or distribution without markup); the motivated flow persists, and the delayed price response arrives over the following quarter (volume as a signal about information quality: Blume, Easley & O'Hara; the volume-return interaction separates information-motivated from hedging flow: Llorente, Michaely, Saar & Wang). When participation is high AND price has already made a large move, the flow is attention-chasing and the sector is relatively over-owned, so subsequent relative drift is flat to negative. The anchor is therefore a participation-quality interaction (volume x follow-through), whose primary hypothesis leg is the long absorption side. It is not a price-shock reversal: no leg is selected on the sign or size of returns alone - the conditioning event is abnormal participation, and the short side is the crowding mirror inside that event. It is equally not momentum: past returns are never ranked.
mechanism.why_after_cost_information: Same slow cadence as a quarterly book: ~3.8/yr two-way turnover, ~38 bps/yr base drag (~76 bps/yr stress). The absorption/crowding differential documented at single-name level is measured in percent per annum at quarterly horizons, leaving an order-of-magnitude margin over the cost drag if the effect survives at liquid-ETF granularity; whether it does is the test, not an assumption.
mechanism.falsifiable_prediction: Sign prediction: among top-participation sectors, the unconfirmed (small trailing price move) minus confirmed (large trailing price move) spread is positive after costs - equivalently the anchor (long top-shock/unconfirmed 3, short top-shock/confirmed 3, dollar-neutral) has positive after-cost expectancy, positive risk-matched excess in >= 2/3 folds, and overall incremental alpha > 0, while the price-only quietness control must NOT reproduce it. If the anchor and the volume-free control earn indistinguishable alpha, the participation-quality mechanism is falsified: quietness alone, not volume conditioning, would explain the return.

primary_sources: Blume, L., Easley, D., & O'Hara, M. (1994). Market Statistics and Technical Analysis: The Role of Volume. Journal of Finance, 49(1), 153-181.
Llorente, G., Michaely, R., Saar, G., & Wang, J. (2002). Dynamic Volume-Return Relation of Individual Stocks. Review of Financial Studies, 15(4), 1005-1040.
Chordia, T., Subrahmanyam, A., & Anshuman, V. R. (2001). Trading Activity and Expected Stock Returns. Journal of Financial Economics, 59(1), 3-32.

files_and_fields.{SYM}_none_p1.json for each of SPY, XLB,: fields datetime, close, volume (raw as-traded); dollar volume DV_s(u) = close_s(u) * volume_s(u) as a declared price-level feature on the authorized raw path; the volume field of _all files is NOT used
files_and_fields.{SYM}_all_p1.json for the 11 sector ETFs: fields datetime, close (split+dividend adjusted) for leg/spread total returns and for the 21-session cumulative follow-through measure follow_s(t) = |adj_close_s(t)/adj_close_s(t-20) - 1|
files_and_fields.SPY_all_p1.json: fields datetime, close (adjusted) used only as the benchmark context denominator; SPY never held, never a feature

authorized_pit_inputs.screening_window: S0 2018-04-04..2025-07-31 only; max scored date <= 2025-07-31; S1 rows never read
authorized_pit_inputs.warmup: 252-session lookback for the shock plus 21 sessions for follow-through (max total 252), drawn from the 2076 pre-S0 sessions; within the warmup allowance
authorized_pit_inputs.explicitly_not_used: intraday bars, fundamentals, earnings calendars, borrow/short interest, ETF holdings, institutional flows, options/implied vol, any network or paid data; _none series never used for return computation

universe_and_schedule.universe: the 11 sector ETFs {XLB, XLC, XLE, XLF, XLI, XLK, XLP, XLRE, XLU, XLV, XLY}; SPY never traded; fixed availability rule: XLC enters the split/rank set only from the first decision session where its full 252-session warmup exists (~2019-06, derived deterministically from the snapshot calendar); before that the set is the 10 available sectors
universe_and_schedule.decision_clock: per fold, every 63rd SPY session starting at the fold's first scored session (offsets 0, 63, 126, ...), decision on that session's PIT close; ~10 decision slots per fold, 30 total across S0
universe_and_schedule.holding_period: 63 sessions per decision book, weights fixed between decision slots; force-flat at every fold boundary per baseline invariants
universe_and_schedule.fill_clock: next allowed session after the decision session, per baseline invariants fill convention (no same-session fill)
universe_and_schedule.book_shape: gross 1.0, net 0.0, cash 1.0; 6 non-CASH legs per decision (3 long, 3 short), with the deterministic completion rule below if a side is short of members

anchor: At decision session t (PIT close): (1) shock_s(t) = mean(DV_s, t-20..t) / mean(DV_s, t-251..t-21) (252-session total lookback). (2) follow_s(t) = |adj_close_s(t)/adj_close_s(t-20) - 1|. (3) Split eligible sectors at the cohort median of follow: unconfirmed := {follow <= median}, confirmed := {follow > median} (the median value itself goes to unconfirmed; deterministic). (4) Among unconfirmed, long the 3 highest-shock sectors at +1/6 each; among confirmed, short the 3 highest-shock sectors at -1/6 each; ties within a side broken by ticker alphabetical ascending. (5) Deterministic completion rule if a side has fewer than 3 members after the split (possible only under exact median ties): build n-versus-n books with n = min(3, side sizes) and weights +/-1/(2n), gross stays 1.0; at least 1 non-CASH leg is always present, satisfying the min-positions invariant. Weights fixed until the next decision slot; fills at the next allowed session; force-flat at fold boundaries. Single fixed rule; no parameter menu.
neighbour: Same anchor construction with one fixed change: the follow-through window extends from 21 to 42 sessions (follow42_s(t) = |adj_close_s(t)/adj_close_s(t-41) - 1|); the shock, split, ranking, tie and completion rules are unchanged. Fixed single variant probing the horizon of the same mechanism: if absorption genuinely reflects persistent motivated flow, the quieter, slower follow-through gauge should also carry positive risk-matched spread alpha. Not a rescue of any forbidden family: the construction conditions on participation quality, contains no return-sign leg and no trend term.

causal_negative_control.control: Price-only quietness control: identical surface form (3v3 dollar-neutral book, per-fold quarterly decision slots, 63-session holding, same tie rules) but built without any volume input: long the 3 eligible sectors with the lowest follow_s(t), short the 3 with the highest follow_s(t).
causal_negative_control.must_not_carry_if_causal_story_true: If participation quality (the volume x follow-through interaction) is the causal ingredient, quietness of price alone - with no abnormal-participation screen - must not earn the spread; the anchor's alpha must exceed this control's for volume to be the operative conditioning variable.
causal_negative_control.preregistered_falsification_rule: The control refutes the mechanism if control after-cost expectancy > 0 AND |control incremental alpha| >= 0.5 x anchor incremental alpha (mirror of the frozen control_alpha_abs_ratio_lt 0.5 gate at anchor scale). A negative anchor with a worse control also rejects the anchor family per the frozen negative-result rule. This control additionally guards the anti-rescue boundary: if quietness alone reproduces the anchor, the anchor is a price-shock artefact and is rejected as such.

factor_alpha_test: Per the frozen benchmark contract: incremental alpha = arm return - risk-matched SPY context, with this arm's declared frozen risk-match scale of 0.5 (long-leg gross exposure of the dollar-neutral book, applied ex ante to the SPY total-return path; realized volatility never substituted post hoc). Evaluated per fold and overall; gates: risk-matched excess positive in >= 2/3 folds and overall incremental alpha > 0. Sector beta is plausible (sector-ETF legs), so the authorized equal-weight sector factor is added: daily OLS r_arm = a + b1*r_SPY + b2*r_EW_sector + eps per fold and over S0; report annualized residualized alpha and both betas. The anchor must retain positive residual alpha after sector-factor neutralization. Realized SPY beta should be ~0 by construction; a materially nonzero beta is a design-failure flag. Raw PnL is never accepted as alpha.

costs_and_turnover.cost_schedule: 10 bps per side per fill (base), 20 bps per side (stress rerun), charged exactly once per fill per the frozen no-double-charge invariant
costs_and_turnover.expected_turnover: Frozen convention sum(abs(delta_weight)) over non-CASH legs, annualized two-way. Base case ~1 leg pair replaced per decision -> 0.67 two-way per decision x ~4.04 decisions/yr ~= 2.7/yr, plus initial build and 3 fold-boundary rebuilds ~= +1.1/yr -> ~3.8/yr two-way.
costs_and_turnover.why_inside_ceiling: Base estimate ~3.8/yr is inside the frozen 6.0 two-way/yr ceiling with ~35% headroom: participation-shock membership is persistent at quarterly cadence and the median split moves slowly, so leg churn is ~1 leg per side per decision rather than wholesale replacement. Adverse case (2+2 legs replaced every decision) computes to ~6.4/yr and would breach the ceiling; this is preregistered as an accepted falsification surface, not a tuning target.
costs_and_turnover.cost_drag: ~38 bps/yr base, ~76 bps/yr at stress; the hypothesized within-participation absorption differential must clear this drag after costs.

sample_size_floor: ~10 decision periods per fold (63-session cadence, offsets 0..567 within fold spans of ~607-619 sessions) and 30 total scheduled across S0; meets the frozen floors (>=5 per fold, >=30 total) exactly with zero slack: any voided slot drops the arm below the floor and it is scored ineligible, not re-timed. The median split never voids a decision (both sides always have members under the deterministic tie rule, and the completion rule preserves >=1 non-CASH leg). Profit factor is computed over the 30 decision-level PnLs under the frozen position-PF convention.
drop_one_design: Drop-one-ETF: rerun the full construction excluding the single max-contribution symbol by cumulative PnL; because removing a symbol can change both the median split and both rankings, the entire split is re-derived from scratch, so survival is a genuine mechanism re-test rather than a position deletion. Meaningfulness is protected by rank/split churn across periods (no single ETF owns a leg permanently) and by the frozen 35% ETF positive-PnL-share gate. Drop-one-fold: min over folds of expectancy with that fold removed, survival requires min > 0; with ~10 decisions per fold, single-fold concentration also trips the frozen fold-positive-share <= 0.5 gate.
failure_interpretation: A reject (after-cost expectancy <= 0, incremental alpha <= 0, price-only control reproduction, ceiling breach, or drop-one failure) means the participation-quality interaction - abnormal volume without price follow-through versus confirmed volume - has no after-cost cross-sectional pricing content at sector-ETF granularity over quarterly horizons: absorption/crowding differentials measurable in single-name studies do not survive at liquid-ETF granularity with daily OHLCV. The abnormal-volume-without-followthrough mechanism class closes for this universe; follow-through-window, split-side and leg-count variants are pre-declared rescue and ineligible. A reject in which the volume-free quietness control performs comparably additionally localizes the failure: daily cohort data cannot separate participation quality from price quietness, which is informative for the whole volume-conditioning class.
source_to_test_map: 1. Blume, Easley & O'Hara (1994): volume is a signal about the quality/informativeness of price moves -> implementation steps: (i) compute DV_s from raw close x volume; (ii) shock_s(t) = 21-session mean / 231-session prior mean as the abnormal-participation screen that gates both book sides.

2. Llorente, Michaely, Saar & Wang (2002): the volume-return interaction separates information-motivated from hedging/speculative flow -> implementation steps: (iii) follow_s(t) = 21-session absolute adjusted return as the follow-through gauge; (iv) median split into unconfirmed/confirmed; (v) long top-shock/unconfirmed 3 vs short top-shock/confirmed 3, dollar-neutral, quarterly.

3. Chordia, Subrahmanyam & Anshuman (2001): trading activity carries cross-sectional expected-return content -> implementation steps: (vi) market neutralization via frozen risk-match scale 0.5 plus SPY + EW-sector factor OLS; (vii) price-only quietness control and stale-free feature check that no ranking input is a return sign or trend statistic (reported at implementation time for the A7-N novelty audit).

implementation_estimate.breakdown: 3.0d shares SFV4-A5-H1 infrastructure (loader, scheduler, book executor, tests) plus 0.5d for the follow-through median split with byte-deterministic tie and completion rules, the volume-free control book, and split golden fixtures
implementation_estimate.risk_notes: Median tie-handling and the side-shortage completion rule must be byte-deterministic and mutation-tested; the control must provably exclude all volume inputs (a no-volume mutation test is required); PIT guards identical to H1 (windows end at the decision session); no resource concerns (12 symbols, ~1842 S0 sessions, serial execution).

outcome_blind_attestation.statement: I did not read per-arm V2/V3 outcomes; this proposal was written before any V4 scoring
